t: Cyrus began as a vassal king of Anshan under the Medes and by 550 BCE had overthrown his overlord and grandfather Astyages.
The conquests of Lydia and, in 539 BCE, of Babylon gave him the largest empire the world had seen to that point, stretching from Asia Minor to the Indus River.
Babylonian, Jewish and Greek sources remember him as a tolerant ruler, though historians read the Cyrus Cylinder as traditional royal propaganda and not as a charter of human rights.
dyk: The Book of Isaiah calls Cyrus anointed by Yahweh, a "messiah"; he is the only non-Jewish figure to be revered in this capacity.
ev: Cyrus is born to Cambyses I, King of Anshan, and Mandane, daughter of the Median king Astyages
He succeeds his father as king, still under Median overlordship
After at least three years of hostilities he captures Ecbatana and overthrows the Median kingdom
He defeats Croesus, occupies Sardis and conquers the Lydian kingdom
His army routs the Babylonians at Opis and he enters Babylon
He crosses the Hindu Kush and collects tribute from the Indus cities
He dies around December and is succeeded by his son Cambyses II

f.born: c. 600 BCE, son of Cambyses I, King of Anshan, and Mandane, daughter of Astyages, King of Media
f.died: Around December 530 BCE; the accounts conflict: killed in battle with the Massagetae (Herodotus), with the Derbices (Ctesias) or with the Dahae (Berossus), or dead peacefully at his capital (Xenophon)
f.role: King of Anshan from 559 BCE under Median overlordship; King of Persia and of Media after the fall of Ecbatana in 550 BCE; King of Babylon, King of Sumer and Akkad and King of the Four Corners of the World from 539 BCE
f.known: Founding the Achaemenid Empire; the conquests of Media, Lydia and the Neo-Babylonian Empire; the Cyrus Cylinder; the return of the Jews from the Babylonian captivity; tolerance of local customs and religions; government through satraps; his tomb at Pasargadae
